pass_a_gloss: [...] grazing flocks of shepherds, that is, of the unclean spirits. Thus also the blessed David, making the words as about Israel as a vineyard, to the God Saviour of all: A vine, he says, you moved out of Egypt, you cast out nations, and planted it. Then he adds, saying: Why did you pull down its hedge, and all those passing along the road gather its grapes? A boar from a thicket ravaged it, and a solitary wild [beast] grazed it down. For in the same manner as the owners throw aside the parts of their lands gone barren, and there is no account to them, even if every damage should be brought upon them, thus also our virtue-loving God lets go a soul, and shows it bare of all sparing, if it should become empty of the fruits toward good-doing. [Lemma, Isaiah 32:15-18:] Until a Spirit comes upon you from on high. And Chermel will be a desert, and Chermel will be reckoned into a thicket. And judgment will rest in the desert, and righteousness will dwell in Carmel. And the works of righteousness will be peace, and righteousness will hold rest, and they will be trusting until the age; and his people will dwell in a city of peace, and will dwell in it trusting, and will rest with wealth. He makes clear also the time at which the race from Israel that disobeyed will be empty of the spiritual fruitfulness. For he moves the discourse onto, I mean, those who have honoured our Lord Jesus Christ with their obediences, and have been cleansed through the faith in him, and have come to be in sharing of the Holy Spirit. For the things announced beforehand will be, he says, and Israel will be laid waste through the unruliness, until a Spirit comes upon you from on high. For as we read in the Acts of the holy apostles: They were all gathered at the same place, about the days of the holy Pentecost. And behold there came suddenly from heaven a sound as of a violent wind being borne, and it filled the house where they were gathered; and there appeared to them tongues being divided as of fire, and they sat upon each one of them, and they began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit was giving them to utter. When then, he says, the Spirit of God from above and from on high comes upon you who believe, then also Chermel will be desert. And the Chermel, or Carmel, is an all-great mountain in Judaea, and thick-haired with dense woodland. He likens then both Jerusalem itself and all the country around the house to Chermel, inasmuch as it also had the multitude of the inhabitants countless. But it will be, he says, desert, and will be reckoned into a thicket. And thicket he calls the wild wood, whose use is for burning. For the untamed of the trees are cut out, and flame [the section breaks off mid-word].
pass_b_english: …the flocks of shepherds, that is, of the unclean spirits. So too the blessed David, framing his words as about Israel as a vineyard, says to God the Savior of all: “You brought a vine out of Egypt; You drove out nations and planted it” (Psalm 80:8). Then he adds: “Why have You broken down its hedge, so that all who pass along the way pluck its fruit? The boar out of the forest has ravaged it, and the solitary wild beast has fed on it” (Psalm 80:12-13).

For just as owners neglect the parts of their lands that have gone barren, and take no thought for them even if every kind of damage comes upon them, so too our God, who loves virtue, lets a soul go and leaves it stripped of all His sparing care, if it becomes empty of the fruits that make for good works.

“Until a Spirit from on high comes upon you. And Chermel will be a wilderness, and Chermel will be counted as a forest. And judgment will rest in the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in Carmel. And the works of righteousness will be peace, and righteousness will hold rest, and they will be confident for ever. And His people will dwell in a city of peace, and will dwell there in confidence, and will rest with wealth” (Isaiah 32:15-18).

He makes clear also the time at which the disobedient race from Israel will be empty of spiritual fruitfulness. For he turns the discourse, I mean, toward those who have honored our Lord Jesus Christ by their ready obedience, who have been cleansed through faith in Him and have come to share in the Holy Spirit. For what was foretold will come to pass, he says, and Israel will be laid waste for its unruliness, until a Spirit from on high comes upon you.

For as we read in the Acts of the holy apostles: “They were all gathered together in one place about the days of holy Pentecost. And suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of a mighty wind rushing, and it filled the house where they were gathered; and there appeared to them tongues dividing, as of fire, and they sat on each one of them, and they began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance” (Acts 2:1-4).

So when, he says, the Spirit of God from above and from on high comes upon you who believe, then Chermel too will be a wilderness. Chermel, or Carmel, is a very large mountain in Judea, thickly covered with dense woodland. So he likens to Chermel both Jerusalem itself and all the country around it, since it too had a countless multitude of inhabitants.
But it will be, he says, a wilderness, and will be counted as a forest. By forest he means wild woodland, which is of use for burning. For the untamed trees are cut down, and flame…

choices.why: Psalm 80:13 Septuagint μονιός, a lone wild animal.
ἀνίημι, to let go or give up; God withdraws his care from a barren soul.
φειδώ is sparing or protective care.
The Septuagint form is kept in the lemma; Cyril then identifies it with Carmel.
Israel is laid waste because it threw off the reins.
